annotations.title: Check a structure before using it

description: Check what a structure is before using it, above all a SMILES you wrote or recalled yourself. For each structure: formula, masses, canonical SMILES, InChI, InChIKey, how many stereocentres and E/Z double bonds are set and which are open (atom numbers from 1, in input order), and warnings (open stereo, charges that do not cancel, atoms over their valence with as_written). With `compare_to`: identical, enantiomers, diastereomers, same skeleton with stereo not set, same compound by InChIKey, constitutional isomers, or different. Calculated, not looked up, except a name at PubChem. An unreadable structure is refused with the reason. Not for a reaction's balance (use analyze) or a figure (use draw).

as_written.description: Draw atoms that have too many bonds instead of refusing the structure. Default false.

compare_is_name.description: True when `compare_to` is a compound name to look up at PubChem. Default false.

compare_to.description: A second structure to compare with: SMILES, InChI, a molfile, or a name with compare_is_name. E.g. your SMILES as `input` and the name of the compound you mean here.

input.description: The structure as text: SMILES, reaction SMILES (reactants>agents>products), InChI, a molfile, RXN, SD file, CDXML, CML or Marvin text, or a Lone Pair drawing (the JSON from an earlier result, or the SVG text of an earlier figure).

name.description: Set to true when `input` is a compound name (e.g. "aspirin") rather than a structure. The name is sent to PubChem to find the structure; this is the only network call the server makes. Short text that is valid SMILES (such as "CO") is read as SMILES, with a note, and not sent. Default false.
